chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Bukayr, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no khums (or zakat) in precious stones and their like, even if they are numerous.

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And if a man leaves with his family an allowance for the years, and it reaches the amount upon which zakat is obligatory, then if he is present, zakat is obligatory upon him for it; and if he is absent, there is no zakat upon him. This is indicated by what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: Is zakat obligatory on precious stones and stored provisions for family?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that 'jawhar' (precious stones and gems) is exempt from zakat, distinguishing it from gold and silver. Shaykh al-Tusi adds a practical legal nuance: provisions left for family are subject to zakat only if the owner is present to manage them, but exempt if he is absent, reflecting the principle of ease in financial obligations. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining zakat liability on non-monetary assets and stored goods.
